4e1cdec9989b91f2f0f84298efa02bbf8802fe76.summary: Both passages give the same instruction to pick the narrowest test level: unit tests for pure logic, integration tests for module boundaries and persistence, end-to-end tests only for critical whole-system journeys.

passages.text:
- Choose the narrowest test level that proves the behavior: unit tests for
  pure logic, integration tests for module boundaries and persistence, and
  end-to-end tests for critical user journeys. Do not turn every test into a
  slow end-to-end test.

- Use focused unit tests for pure logic and isolated components, integration
  tests for real module boundaries, and end-to-end tests only for workflows
  that need the complete system. Keep the test level visible in the test
  location and name according to the repository convention.

5478e71bc98c8e9b1630a998b9956cd392f8cfee.summary: All three passages instruct the same thing: run the repository's configured formatter, linter/static checks, type checker or compiler, and relevant tests before handing off, rather than substituting other tooling or claiming unrun checks.

passages.text:
- Use the project's configured formatter, linter, compiler, and test runner.
  At minimum, TypeScript changes SHOULD pass `tsc --noEmit` (or the project's
  equivalent), linting, formatting checks, and the relevant tests. Do not
  replace repository tooling with a personal global installation.

- Before handing off a change, run the project's formatter, linter, type
  checker, and relevant tests. When no project-specific commands exist, a
  reasonable baseline is `python -m compileall`, the configured test command,
  and the configured static checks; do not claim checks passed without running
  them.

625232ff4edbe7ea1165ceb0969aa7ae6435f95c.summary: Both passages instruct that tests cover failure behavior as well as success, naming the same cases: malformed input, missing values or configuration, expected errors, and authorization or persistence failures.

passages.text:
- Test both successful and failure behavior, including malformed input,
  missing values, rejected promises, cancellation or timeout behavior, and
  authorization or persistence failures where they matter.

- Exercise successful and failure behavior, especially malformed input,
  missing configuration, expected exceptions, authorization decisions,
  persistence failures, and resource cleanup. Assert the exception type and
  meaningful details without over-specifying incidental message formatting.

78dc98847c5d7400de0afc038ce631cbc60c6a16.summary: All three passages state the same rule: test observable behavior and public contracts rather than private implementation details, so a contract-preserving refactor does not force test rewrites.

passages.text:
- Test observable behavior and public contracts, not the exact arrangement of
  private functions or implementation details. A refactor that preserves the
  contract should not require rewriting the test suite.

- Test observable behavior and public contracts, not private implementation
  details. A refactor that preserves the contract should not require rewriting
  the tests.

- Add or update tests with behavior changes. Test observable behavior and
  important failure modes, not private implementation details. A test is
  useful only when it can fail for a real regression.

7b1d3e1ee85685cb48939439ab27f5ec377f43b1.summary: Both passages instruct that external input be validated or parsed once at the trust boundary and passed inward as a domain type that internal code may rely on.

passages.text:
- Validate data at trust boundaries: HTTP responses, request bodies, files,
  environment variables, message queues, and browser storage are not made
  safe by a TypeScript type assertion. Assertions have no runtime effect.
  Parse or validate the data once, then pass the resulting domain type inward.

- Validate external input at the boundary and convert it to a domain shape
  once. Internal functions SHOULD be able to rely on their stated types and
  invariants rather than repeatedly defending against every possible input.

b0928e1237908e81ce32dec652b1dd7d8d645bd4.summary: Both passages instruct that the project's own test and static-check commands be used and that test discovery of the intended files be confirmed rather than assumed.

passages.text:
- Use the repository's configured runner, environment, formatter, linter, and
  compiler. A change should include relevant tests and pass the project's
  normal test command; do not assume that a test file is discovered unless the
  runner configuration confirms it.

- Run the project's normal test and static-check commands. At minimum, make
  sure the test runner discovers the intended files and that a deliberately
  broken assertion makes the test fail during test development.

c087a2d64bb582e4a92f0e0c7f5e987ad36e7c5f.summary: Both passages give the same instruction not to introduce an abstraction merely because two pieces of code look similar or might be reusable, and to accept a little local duplication instead.

passages.text:
- Do not abstract two things merely because they look similar. First establish
  that they have the same behavior, ownership, change reason, and invariants.
  A small amount of local duplication is preferable to a premature generic
  abstraction that couples unrelated callers.

- Do not introduce speculative abstractions or abstractions solely because a
  change might be reusable. A concrete, domain-owned abstraction that
  improves cohesion, removes real duplication, or makes a branch independently
  testable is not premature; use it when the code evidence supports it, even
  when the task did not name the extraction. Keep it as small as possible.

c7e6f241fb50528be272c1ce2f50a1de2a3feda5.summary: Both passages give the same mocking rule: keep mocks narrow, mock an external boundary only when isolation or determinism requires it, and do not mock the code under test so heavily that the test only proves its own wiring.

passages.text:
- Keep mocks narrow and behavior-oriented. Mock an external boundary when
  isolation or determinism requires it, but do not mock the unit's own logic
  so thoroughly that the test only verifies the mock wiring.

- Keep mocks narrow and purposeful. Mock an external boundary when isolation
  or determinism requires it, but do not mock the code under test so heavily
  that the test only proves its own setup.

d92572fdcd86a53939f9bd11050d62966b024f00.summary: Both bullets state the same prohibition on calling `asyncio.run()` from code that is already running inside an event loop.

passages.text:
- Keep async code non-blocking. Do not call blocking I/O or CPU-heavy work
  directly from an event loop; use an appropriate async API or explicitly move
  the work to a worker. Do not call `asyncio.run()` from code that may already
  be running inside an event loop.

- For async code, test coroutines with the project's supported async test
  tooling. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside an already-running event loop,
  and do not use sleeps to wait for concurrency. Test cancellation, timeout,
  cleanup, and ordering assumptions when they affect correctness.

f33fac02539e620b84f83f37e8441e63b983952d.summary: Both passages require deterministic, isolated tests with the same list of prohibitions and remedies: no real network, shared mutable state, uncontrolled randomness or arbitrary sleeps, and explicit control of time, randomness and external clients.

passages.text:
- Keep tests deterministic and isolated. Avoid real network calls, shared
  mutable state, random values without a controlled seed, and arbitrary timer
  sleeps. Control time, randomness, environment, and external clients at
  explicit boundaries.

- Keep each test independent and deterministic. Avoid order dependence,
  shared mutable module state, real network services, the current time, and
  arbitrary sleeps. Use temporary directories, controlled clocks, seeded
  randomness, and explicit fakes or mocks at external boundaries.
